DEFAULT_JUDGE_MODEL = "claude-sonnet-5-5"
RATE_LIMIT_RE = re.compile(r"rate.?limit|429|overloaded|too many requests|throttl", re.I)


class ModelPinError(RuntimeError):
    """A result was produced under different (or missing) pinned models: never mix, so abort."""


class EvalInfraError(RuntimeError):
    """Infrastructure failure running an eval (no verdict). kind: rate_limit | timeout | crash."""

    def __init__(self, kind: str, msg: str = ""):
        super().__init__(f"{kind}: {msg}")
        self.kind = kind


class BuildError(RuntimeError):
    pass


@dataclass
class RunResult:
    case_id: str
    status: str  # pass | fail | skipped | error
    trace_id: str | None = None
    agent_model: str | None = None
    judge_model: str | None = None
    reason: str = ""


@dataclass
class CaseRequest:
    workdir: Path
    sha: str
    case: str
    repeats: int
    run_id: str
    env: dict[str, str]
    timeout: float


class EvalExecutor(Protocol):
    """Runs one case `repeats` times at a checked-out commit. Tests supply a fake; production uses SubprocessExecutor."""

    def run_case(self, req: CaseRequest) -> list[RunResult]: ...


def parse_report(report: dict) -> list[RunResult]:
    if report.get("schema_version") != 1:
        raise EvalInfraError("crash", f"unsupported schema_version {report.get('schema_version')!r}")
    return [RunResult(case_id=r["case_id"], status=r["status"], trace_id=r.get("trace_id"),
                      agent_model=r.get("agent_model") or report.get("agent_model"),
                      judge_model=r.get("judge_model") or report.get("judge_model"),
                      reason=r.get("reason") or "")
            for r in report.get("results", [])]


class SubprocessExecutor:
    def __init__(self, eval_cmd: list[str] | None = None):
        self.eval_cmd = eval_cmd or ["uv", "run", "python", "-m", "evals"]

    def run_case(self, req: CaseRequest) -> list[RunResult]:
        cmd = [*self.eval_cmd, "run", "--json", "--isolate", "--suite", "all", "--cases", req.case,
               "--repeats", str(req.repeats), "--commit", req.sha, "--run-id", req.run_id]
        try:
            p = subprocess.run(cmd, cwd=req.workdir, env=req.env, capture_output=True, text=True,
                               timeout=req.timeout)
        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired as e:
            raise EvalInfraError("timeout", f"{req.case} exceeded {req.timeout}s") from e
        try:
            return parse_report(json.loads(p.stdout))
        except json.JSONDecodeError:
            tail = (p.stderr or p.stdout)[-500:]
            kind = "rate_limit" if RATE_LIMIT_RE.search(tail) else "crash"
            raise EvalInfraError(kind, f"exit {p.returncode}, no JSON report: {tail}")


@dataclass
class RunnerConfig:
    cases: list[str]
    repeats: int = 3  # R, initial repeats per case
    max_repeats: int = 12  # cap for escalation
    workers: int = 4
    timeout: float = 600.0
    install_cmd: list[str] | None = field(default_factory=lambda: ["uv", "sync"])
    install_timeout: float = 600.0
    max_retries: int = 3
    backoff: float = 2.0
    models: dict[str, str] = field(default_factory=lambda: {
        "agent_model": os.environ.get("AGENT_MODEL") or DEFAULT_AGENT_MODEL,
        "judge_model": os.environ.get("JUDGE_MODEL") or DEFAULT_JUDGE_MODEL})
    # Confidence band: pass_rate >= good_min -> good, <= bad_max -> bad, else uncertain (escalate repeats).
    good_min: float = 0.85
    bad_max: float = 0.5
    classify: Callable[[float, int], str] | None = None  # hook: (pass_rate, n_runs) -> good|bad|uncertain
    env_file: str | None = None  # KEY=VALUE lines (API keys) injected into eval subprocesses; never logged
    worktree_root: str | None = None


def default_classify(cfg: RunnerConfig) -> Callable[[float, int], str]:
    def f(rate: float, n: int) -> str:
        return "good" if rate >= cfg.good_min else "bad" if rate <= cfg.bad_max else "uncertain"
    return f


@contextlib.contextmanager
def worktree(repo: Path, sha: str, root: str | None = None) -> Iterator[Path]:
    """Detached worktree at sha in a temp dir; always removed and pruned, even on error."""
    tmp = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="agentbisect-wt-", dir=root))
    path = tmp / "wt"
    try:
        subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(repo), "worktree", "add", "--detach", str(path), sha],
                       capture_output=True, text=True, check=True)
        yield path
    finally:
        subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(repo), "worktree", "remove", "--force", str(path)], capture_output=True)
        shutil.rmtree(tmp, ignore_errors=True)
        subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(repo), "worktree", "prune"], capture_output=True)


def _load_env_file(path: str | None) -> dict[str, str]:
    out: dict[str, str] = {}

            if line and not line.startswith("#") and "=" in line:
                k, v = line.split("=", 1)
                out[k.strip()] = v.strip().strip("'\"")

=========== ROLES.md
# Roles, pinned models, isolation

Five separate roles. They must not share context.

| # | Role | What it is | Model |
| - | ---- | ---------- | ----- |
| 1 | History builder | A Claude Code session with `entire` on that writes support-agent-demo's ~20 commits (the seeded regressions). | its own session model |
| 2 | Support agent | The runtime lab rat, exercised by every eval. | PINNED Haiku: `AGENT_MODEL`, default `claude-haiku-5-5` |
| 3 | Eval judge | Grades replies against a rubric, only after deterministic checks pass and only when a rubric exists. | PINNED, smarter than the agent: `JUDGE_MODEL`, default `claude-sonnet-5-5` |
| 4 | AgentBisect | The tool: bisects the history using eval results. (Not built yet.) | n/a |
| 5 | Fixer | A fresh agent that repairs the culprit commit. | its own session model |

## Pinning rules (implemented in support-agent-demo `evals/models.py`, `evals/judge.py`, `evals/harness.py`)

- Tier order: haiku < sonnet < opus/fable. The judge must be a different model than the agent, not haiku-tier,
  and a higher tier than the agent. Violations raise `ModelConfigError` (CLI exits non-zero, `LLMJudge` refuses
  to construct).
- Judge: temperature 0, strict rubric, structured JSON verdict (per-criterion pass/fail + reason), overall
  `passed` computed in code as all-criteria-pass, `rubric_sha256` and `judge_model` recorded in each verdict.
- `agent_model` and `judge_model` are written into every eval report, every case result and every baseline.
  The harness refuses to run against a baseline, and `compare_reports` refuses to compare reports, whose pinned
  models differ or are missing, so a model cannot silently drift between commits. Changing a pin means
  recalibrating the baseline and re-running, never mixing.
- Tests use fake providers only; no live Claude call has been made (no API key at build time).

## Isolation rules

- History builder and AgentBisect builder are separate sessions that know nothing about each other. The history
  builder never sees AgentBisect, the eval ground truth, or this repo.
- The Fixer is fresh and knows nothing about how bugs were planted. Its context contains ONLY: the culprit diff,
  the intent of that change, and the failing eval evidence. It never receives the history-builder briefs, the
  planted-regression names (R1/R2/R3), or any `breaks`/`intent_for` metadata.
- Ground truth is kept out of the target repo. `breaks` (R1/R2/R3/control) and `intent_for` were removed from
  support-agent-demo `evals/cases.jsonl` (the loader rejects them) and live in
  `evidence/ground_truth.json` in this repo. It is for scoring AgentBisect's answer, and must be stripped from
  anything handed to the support agent, judge or Fixer. Evidence passed to the Fixer must be built from eval
  results (which carry no `breaks`), not from this file.

"""Run the target repo's evals at a commit, in an isolated git worktree, with retries, caching and flaky handling.

Target contract (support-agent-demo evals/README.md): `python -m evals run --json --isolate --cases X
--repeats N --commit SHA --run-id ID` prints a schema_version 1 report on stdout. AgentBisect never reads the
target's ground truth; it only sees these results.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import contextlib
import json
import os
import re
import shutil
import subprocess
import tempfile
import threading
import time
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Callable, Iterator, Protocol

from .models import CommitResult
from .state import BUILD_CASE, VerdictCache
from .tracing import step_span

DEFAULT_AGENT_MODEL = "claude-haiku-5-5"
DEFAULT_JUDGE_MODEL = "claude-sonnet-5-5"
RATE_LIMIT_RE = re.compile(r"rate.?limit|429|overloaded|too many requests|throttl", re.I)


class ModelPinError(RuntimeError):
    """A result was produced under different (or missing) pinned models: never mix, so abort."""


class EvalInfraError(RuntimeError):
    """Infrastructure failure running an eval (no verdict). kind: rate_limit | timeout | crash."""

    def __init__(self, kind: str, msg: str = ""):
        super().__init__(f"{kind}: {msg}")
        self.kind = kind


class BuildError(RuntimeError):
    pass


@dataclass
class RunResult:
    case_id: str
    status: str  # pass | fail | skipped | error
    trace_id: str | None = None
    agent_model: str | None = None
    judge_model: str | None = None
    reason: str = ""


@dataclass
class CaseRequest:
    workdir: Path
    sha: str
    case: str
    repeats: int
    run_id: str
    env: dict[str, str]
    timeout: float


class EvalExecutor(Protocol):
    """Runs one case `repeats` times at a checked-out commit. Tests supply a fake; production uses SubprocessExecutor."""

    def run_case(self, req: CaseRequest) -> list[RunResult]: ...


def parse_report(report: dict) -> list[RunResult]:
    if report.get("schema_version") != 1:
        raise EvalInfraError("crash", f"unsupported schema_version {report.get('schema_version')!r}")
    return [RunResult(case_id=r["case_id"], status=r["status"], trace_id=r.get("trace_id"),
                      agent_model=r.get("agent_model") or report.get("agent_model"),
                      judge_model=r.get("judge_model") or report.get("judge_model"),
                      reason=r.get("reason") or "")
            for r in report.get("results", [])]


class SubprocessExecutor:
    def __init__(self, eval_cmd: list[str] | None = None):
        self.eval_cmd = eval_cmd or ["uv", "run", "python", "-m", "evals"]

    def run_case(self, req: CaseRequest) -> list[RunResult]:
        cmd = [*self.eval_cmd, "run", "--json", "--isolate", "--suite", "all", "--cases", req.case,
               "--repeats", str(req.repeats), "--commit", req.sha, "--run-id", req.run_id]
        try:
            p = subprocess.run(cmd, cwd=req.workdir, env=req.env, capture_output=True, text=True,
                               timeout=req.timeout)
        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired as e:
            raise EvalInfraError("timeout", f"{req.case} exceeded {req.timeout}s") from e
        try:
            return parse_report(json.loads(p.stdout))
        except json.JSONDecodeError:
            tail = (p.stderr or p.stdout)[-500:]
            kind = "rate_limit" if RATE_LIMIT_RE.search(tail) else "crash"
            raise EvalInfraError(kind, f"exit {p.returncode}, no JSON report: {tail}")


@dataclass
class RunnerConfig:
    cases: list[str]
    repeats: int = 3  # R, initial repeats per case
    max_repeats: int = 12  # cap for escalation
    workers: int = 4
    timeout: float = 600.0
    install_cmd: list[str] | None = field(default_factory=lambda: ["uv", "sync"])
    install_timeout: float = 600.0
    max_retries: int = 3
    backoff: float = 2.0
    models: dict[str, str] = field(default_factory=lambda: {
        "agent_model": os.environ.get("AGENT_MODEL") or DEFAULT_AGENT_MODEL,
        "judge_model": os.environ.get("JUDGE_MODEL") or DEFAULT_JUDGE_MODEL})
    # Confidence band: pass_rate >= good_min -> good, <= bad_max -> bad, else uncertain (escalate repeats).
    good_min: float = 0.85
    bad_max: float = 0.5
    classify: Callable[[float, int], str] | None = None  # hook: (pass_rate, n_runs) -> good|bad|uncertain
    env_file: str | None = None  # KEY=VALUE lines (API keys) injected into eval subprocesses; never logged
    worktree_root: str | None = None


def default_classify(cfg: RunnerConfig) -> Callable[[float, int], str]:
    def f(rate: float, n: int) -> str:
        return "good" if rate >= cfg.good_min else "bad" if rate <= cfg.bad_max else "uncertain"
    return f


@contextlib.contextmanager
def worktree(repo: Path, sha: str, root: str | None = None) -> Iterator[Path]:
    """Detached worktree at sha in a temp dir; always removed and pruned, even on error."""
    tmp = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="agentbisect-wt-", dir=root))
    path = tmp / "wt"
    try:
        subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(repo), "worktree", "add", "--detach", str(path), sha],
                       capture_output=True, text=True, check=True)
        yield path
    finally:
        subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(repo), "worktree", "remove", "--force", str(path)], capture_output=True)
        shutil.rmtree(tmp, ignore_errors=True)
        subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(repo), "worktree", "prune"], capture_output=True)


def _load_env_file(path: str | None) -> dict[str, str]:
    out: dict[str, str] = {}
    if path and Path(path).exists():
        for line in Path(path).read_text().splitlines():
            line = line.strip()
            if line and not line.startswith("#") and "=" in line:
                k, v = line.split("=", 1)
                out[k.strip()] = v.strip().strip("'\"")
    return out

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass, field
from typing import Any

STATUSES = ("created", "running", "paused", "failed", "culprit_found", "fixing", "verifying", "reported")
VERDICTS = ("good", "bad", "flaky", "skip")


@dataclass
class RegressionSpec:
    source: str = "trace"  # trace | detection | issue
    bad_trace_id: str | None = None
    good_trace_ids: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    cases: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    held_out: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    predicate: dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)  # {"checks": [...], "rubric": str|None}
    metric: str = "pass_rate"

    def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        return asdict(self)

    @classmethod
    def from_dict(cls, d: dict[str, Any]) -> "RegressionSpec":
        return cls(**d)


@dataclass
class Candidate:
    sha: str
    score: float = 0.0
    reason: str = ""


@dataclass
class Plan:
    divergent_span: str | None = None
    impacted_symbols: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    candidates: list[Candidate] = field(default_factory=list)
    mode: str = "smart"  # smart | plain

    def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        return asdict(self)

    @classmethod
    def from_dict(cls, d: dict[str, Any]) -> "Plan":
        d = dict(d)
        d["candidates"] = [Candidate(**c) for c in d.get("candidates", [])]
        return cls(**d)


@dataclass
class CommitResult:
    """Verdict for one commit: results{sha: verdict, pass_rate, trace_ids} plus flaky/skip detail."""
    verdict: str  # good | bad | flaky | skip
    pass_rate: float | None = None
    trace_ids: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    reason: str = ""  # why skipped / flaky
    executed: int = 0
    repeats: int = 0  # repeats per case actually used (after escalation)
    flaky_cases: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    failing_cases: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    case_stats: dict[str, dict[str, int]] = field(default_factory=dict)  # case -> passes/fails/errors
    from_cache: bool = False

    def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        return asdict(self)

    @classmethod
    def from_dict(cls, d: dict[str, Any]) -> "CommitResult":
        return cls(**d)


@dataclass
class BisectState:
    id: str
    repo: str = ""
    good_sha: str | None = None
    bad_sha: str | None = None
    spec: RegressionSpec | None = None
    plan: Plan | None = None
    results: dict[str, CommitResult] = field(default_factory=dict)
    step: int = 0
    status: str = "created"
    in_flight: dict[str, Any] | None = None  # step started but not completed (set => crashed mid-step)
    context_tokens_per_step: list[dict[str, Any]] = field(default_factory=list)  # {step, label, tokens}
    pinned_models: dict[str, str] = field(default_factory=dict)
    culprit: "CulpritReport | None" = None
    fix_attempts: list["FixAttempt"] = field(default_factory=list)
    created_at: str = ""
    updated_at: str = ""
    error: str | None = None

    def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        return {
            **{k: v for k, v in asdict(self).items()
               if k not in ("spec", "plan", "results", "culprit", "fix_attempts")},
            "spec": self.spec.to_dict() if self.spec else None,
            "plan": self.plan.to_dict() if self.plan else None,
            "results": {s: r.to_dict() for s, r in self.results.items()},
            "culprit": self.culprit.to_dict() if self.culprit else None,
            "fix_attempts": [f.to_dict() for f in self.fix_attempts],
        }

    @classmethod
    def from_dict(cls, d: dict[str, Any]) -> "BisectState":
        d = dict(d)
        d["spec"] = RegressionSpec.from_dict(d["spec"]) if d.get("spec") else None
        d["plan"] = Plan.from_dict(d["plan"]) if d.get("plan") else None
        d["results"] = {s: CommitResult.from_dict(r) for s, r in d.get("results", {}).items()}
        d["culprit"] = CulpritReport.from_dict(d["culprit"]) if d.get("culprit") else None
        d["fix_attempts"] = [FixAttempt.from_dict(f) for f in d.get("fix_attempts", [])]
        return cls(**d)

# Pitstop

**An autonomous pit crew for AI agents.** Point Pitstop at an agent repo. It runs
the agent's evals, reads the neatlogs traces of the failing runs, works out the
root cause, patches the code, re-runs the evals, and keeps the patch only if the
numbers improve. Each accepted fix lands as its own git commit with before/after
metrics and trace ids. Patches that don't help are reverted.

Built for [neatHack](https://neatlogs.com/hackathon) (Oct 10–12, 2026) by team **4'feetus**.

**First real run** ([report](reports/pitstop-1010-2320-db0d.md)): Scout on `claude-haiku`, Pitstop on `claude-sonnet-4.6`, via the hackathon LiteLLM proxy.

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| tasks passing | 0/6 | **6/6** |
| tokens (6 tasks) | 58,879 | **16,302 (-72%)** |
| est. cost per eval run | $0.0697 | **$0.0251 (-64%)** |
| avg latency | 4.6 s | 3.2 s |

Three rounds, three accepted fixes, each its own commit with the evidence that justified it:

1. **Fenced JSON.** Every neatlogs trace ended in `scout.research status=ERROR JSONDecodeError`; the timelines showed answers starting with a markdown code fence. Pitstop stripped fences before parsing (+19 checks).
2. **Context bloat.** `people_search` returned ~50k chars of full profiles into context. Pitstop trimmed it to name/title (0 → 5 tasks pass).
3. **Invented numbers.** The prompt said "never leave a field null", so the model filled zerodha.com's missing funding with 0. Pitstop allowed null for unknown values (5 → 6).

Pitstop spent $0.21 (7 model calls), read 9 neatlogs traces back and ran 7 Entire Graph searches.

## How it works

```
            ┌──────────── evals (pitstop.toml: eval_cmd) ─────────────┐
            ▼                                                          │
  target agent ──traces──▶ neatlogs ──trace API──▶ evidence ─┬▶ DIAGNOSE (claude-sonnet-4.6)
  target repo ──entire graph search──▶ candidate fix sites ───┘
                                                                       │ ranked root-cause hypotheses
                                                                       ▼
            keep + commit ◀── ACCEPT ◀── compare ◀── evals ◀── tests ◀── PATCH (search/replace edits)
            revert        ◀── REJECT ◀──┘                     │
                                     repair once ◀── edit didn't apply / tests failed
```

1. **Evaluate.** Run the target's eval command (declared in its `pitstop.toml`).
   The harness meters every model call itself, so the agent can't hide steps.
2. **Collect evidence.** For each failing task: failed checks, a step-by-step
   timeline (tool calls, arguments, result sizes, errors, tokens per step) and
   the neatlogs spans and detections for that task's trace, read back through the neatlogs trace API.
3. **Localize.** Each failure signal (an exception, a failing tool call, an
   oversized tool result, an invented value) becomes an `entire graph search`
   over the target repo. Only hits in editable files are kept, as candidate fix sites.
4. **Diagnose.** The model returns ranked hypotheses, each citing evidence
   (task, step, failure text), and sees every earlier attempt and why it was rejected.
5. **Patch.** Minimal search/replace edits, limited to files the target marks
   `editable`. Evals and data are read-only, so the agent can't game its own tests.
   If an edit doesn't apply or the unit tests fail, the error goes back to the
   model for one repair attempt.
6. **Verify.** Re-run the evals. Accept only if more tasks pass, or more checks
   pass, or results stay equal with ≥10% fewer tokens, and no passing task
   regresses. Otherwise revert.
7. **Report.** A markdown + JSON report with the before/after table, every
   accepted diff, every rejected attempt and why, and all trace ids.

Pitstop has a hard USD budget (`--budget`) for its own model calls and stops
cleanly (reverting any half-applied patch) when it hits it.

## The patient: Scout

[`patients/scout`](patients/scout) is a small but real tool-using research agent:
company website in, JSON brief out (headcount, funding, founding year, HQ,
leaders), built on Crustdata company and people data. Its eval checks that the
brief parses, names the right company, matches the data source number for
number (no invented values), lists real people, and stays within a token budget.

Scout ships with the faults real agents ship with. Pitstop isn't told what they are.

## Quick start

```bash
python -m venv .venv && .venv/Scripts/activate      # or source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -e .
cp .env.example .env                                 # add LITELLM_API_KEY and NEATLOGS_API_KEY
pitstop doctor --ping
pitstop init-demo                                    # copies Scout into sandbox/scout as a git repo
pitstop eval                                         # baseline
pitstop heal --rounds 4 --budget 1.50                # the pit stop
```

Offline (no keys, scripted models): `pytest -q`.

### Using it on your own agent

Add a `pitstop.toml` to your agent repo:

```toml
[target]
name = "my-agent"
description = "what it does"
eval_cmd = ["{python}", "-m", "evals.run", "--out", "{out}", "--model", "{model}"]
test_cmd = ["{python}", "-m", "pytest", "-q"]
editable = ["agent/*.py", "agent/prompts.py"]
context  = ["evals/run.py"]
```

Your eval command must write JSON with a `summary`

# Suture

An agent that fixes broken agents, and only hands the fix over once an outside check shows it worked.

Built for neatHack, track "Build an agent that works (literally)".

neatlogs finds what broke and can suggest a fix. Suture tests the fix, and only hands it over once a signed outside check shows it worked.

## What it does

You point Suture at an AI agent that sometimes gets things wrong. Suture then:

1. Runs the outside check (StressProof, 12 probes) on the agent and saves the signed "before" report.
2. Reads the failing runs from the agent's neatlogs traces, so it fixes what actually broke, not what it guesses broke.
3. Asks the model for a patch and applies it to a copy of the agent, never the original.
4. Runs the agent's own tests, plus a new test written from the failure that fails on the original code.
5. Puts the patched copy online and runs StressProof again for the signed "after" report.
6. Keeps the fix only if quiet failures (wrong answers that look fine) are 0 and the score did not drop. Otherwise it throws the patch away and tries again, up to 3 times.
7. If a fix is kept, it opens a pull request. It never merges. A person decides.

## One run you can check

Target: Clerk, a small refund-lookup agent (`targets/clerk`). Its first draft answered broken requests with a confident, made-up answer.

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| StressProof score | 75 (PARTIAL) | 92 in the pull request, 100 in the latest re-run |
| Quiet failures | 1 | 0 |
| Attempts used | | 1 of 3 |
| Cost of the fix | | about $0.11 (model about $0.10, two outside checks $0.01) |

The signed reports and the numbers are in `evidence/`. The pull request is [#1](https://github.com/Sireadell/suture/pull/1).

## Try it yourself in one minute

```powershell
python -m venv .venv
.\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
pip install -r requirements.txt
copy .env.example .env      # then fill in your own keys
python -m pytest targets\clerk
python -m suture.loop
```

Open any signed report link in `evidence/scorecard.json`. Each one is a StressProof page anyone can verify.

## How it uses the three event tools

| Tool | Use in Suture |
|---|---|
| neatlogs | Suture traces itself and the target agent. It reads failing runs and its own cost back through the neatlogs command line. |
| Entire | Build sessions are recorded as checkpoints on this repo, linked from the submission. |
| cfo.ai | The business plan: price per accepted fix, cost per fix, revenue and runway. Numbers come from the real run above. |

## What existed before the event

StressProof, the outside checker, is my earlier project (github.com/Sireadell/stressproof). Suture calls it as a service. Everything in this repo (the repair loop, the neatlogs reading, the keep rule, Clerk and the other test agents) was written during the event.

## What this is not

- It does not merge anything. It opens a pull request and stops.
- It does not promise a fix every time. If it cannot prove a fix, it hands back nothing and says so.
- It is not a general bug fixer. It repairs one kind of fault, agents that answer bad input with a confident wrong answer.
- It does not prove the target is perfect. A score of 100 means the 12 probes passed, nothing more.
- Today it has one fully proven target. More are in `targets/` and are not claimed until their runs are in `evidence/`.

## Limits I know about

- neatlogs Fixes is not used yet. The command line has no Fixes command, and connecting GitHub in neatlogs did not work for this project.
- The neatlogs login I have is read-only, so Suture cannot write its verdict back into neatlogs.
- neatlogs cost counts leave out the model's thinking tokens, so Suture also keeps its own counters and reports the larger number.

# Rootline

When an AI support agent starts failing in production, Rootline finds the reasoning mistake in the coding session that caused it, fixes it, and proves the fix.

The patient is a small support agent for Kettle & Co., a fictional tea brand. It is traced in neatlogs. Rootline reads those traces, locates the bad commit, reads the Entire checkpoint of the coding session, applies a fix, and replays the tickets.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  patient[Kettle support agent] --> neatlogs[neatlogs traces]
  neatlogs --> detect[DETECT]
  detect --> locate[LOCATE git and Entire graph]
  locate --> explain[EXPLAIN checkpoints and search]
  explain --> fix[FIX headless agent and Trail]
  fix --> verify[VERIFY replay]
  verify --> report[REPORT]
```

## Setup

Python 3.12 and [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/).

```powershell
uv sync
copy .env.example .env
```

Fill `.env` with `NEATLOGS_API_KEY` and `OPENAI_API_KEY`. Patient model is `gpt-5-mini`. Investigator model is `gpt-5`.

Install Entire, then log in with GitHub:

```powershell
irm https://entire.io/install.ps1 | iex
entire login
```

Install the Entire GitHub App on the repo, then turn on Runners, Auto build on push, and Trails.

## Run

```powershell
uv run python -m evals.run_evals --label baseline
uv run rootline investigate --branch <failing-branch>
uv run rootline resume <run_id>
uv run rootline report <run_id> --open
```

Baseline on commit `71319f7`, 10 October 2026: **24/24** passed. The result file is `evals/out/baseline-71319f7-20261010T135708Z.json`.

## What is still human-operated

- Public GitHub repository and push
- Entire login and repo settings
- neatlogs detections in the dashboard
- cfo.ai plan, after cancelling the paid trial immediately
- One EC2 `t3.small` in `us-east-1` inside `Hackathon_VPC`, later, for watch mode

|---|---|---|
| tasks passing | 0/6 | **6/6** |
| tokens (6 tasks) | 58,879 | **16,302 (-72%)** |
| est. cost per eval run | $0.0697 | **$0.0251 (-64%)** |
| avg latency | 4.6 s | 3.2 s |

Three rounds, three accepted fixes, each its own commit with the evidence that justified it:

1. **Fenced JSON.** Every neatlogs trace ended in `scout.research status=ERROR JSONDecodeError`; the timelines showed answers starting with a markdown code fence. Pitstop stripped fences before parsing (+19 checks).
2. **Context bloat.** `people_search` returned ~50k chars of full profiles into context. Pitstop trimmed it to name/title (0 → 5 tasks pass).
3. **Invented numbers.** The prompt said "never leave a field null", so the model filled zerodha.com's missing funding with 0. Pitstop allowed null for unknown values (5 → 6).

Pitstop spent $0.21 (7 model calls), read 9 neatlogs traces back and ran 7 Entire Graph searches.

## How it works

```
            ┌──────────── evals (pitstop.toml: eval_cmd) ─────────────┐
            ▼                                                          │
  target agent ──traces──▶ neatlogs ──trace API──▶ evidence ─┬▶ DIAGNOSE (claude-sonnet-4.6)
  target repo ──entire graph search──▶ candidate fix sites ───┘
                                                                       │ ranked root-cause hypotheses
                                                                       ▼
            keep + commit ◀── ACCEPT ◀── compare ◀── evals ◀── tests ◀── PATCH (search/replace edits)
            revert        ◀── REJECT ◀──┘                     │
                                     repair once ◀── edit didn't apply / tests failed
```

1. **Evaluate.** Run the target's eval command (declared in its `pitstop.toml`).
   The harness meters every model call itself, so the agent can't hide steps.
2. **Collect evidence.** For each failing task: failed checks, a step-by-step
   timeline (tool calls, arguments, result sizes, errors, tokens per step) and
   the neatlogs spans and detections for that task's trace, read back through the neatlogs trace API.
3. **Localize.** Each failure signal (an exception, a failing tool call, an
   oversized tool result, an invented value) becomes an `entire graph search`
   over the target repo. Only hits in editable files are kept, as candidate fix sites.
4. **Diagnose.** The model returns ranked hypotheses, each citing evidence
   (task, step, failure text), and sees every earlier attempt and why it was rejected.
5. **Patch.** Minimal search/replace edits, limited to files the target marks
   `editable`. Evals and data are read-only, so the agent can't game its own tests.
   If an edit doesn't apply or the unit tests fail, the error goes back to the
   model for one repair attempt.
6. **Verify.** Re-run the evals. Accept only if more tasks pass, or more checks
   pass, or results stay equal with ≥10% fewer tokens, and no passing task
   regresses. Otherwise revert.
7. **Report.** A markdown + JSON report with the before/after table, every
   accepted diff, every rejected attempt and why, and all trace ids.

Pitstop has a hard USD budget (`--budget`) for its own model calls and stops
cleanly (reverting any half-applied patch) when it hits it.

## The patient: Scout

[`patients/scout`](patients/scout) is a small but real tool-using research agent:
company website in, JSON brief out (headcount, funding, founding year, HQ,
leaders), built on Crustdata company and people data. Its eval checks that the
brief parses, names the right company, matches the data source number for
number (no invented values), lists real people, and stays within a token budget.

Scout ships with the faults real agents ship with. Pitstop isn't told what they are.

# Suture

An agent that fixes broken agents, and only hands the fix over once an outside check shows it worked.

Built for neatHack, track "Build an agent that works (literally)".

neatlogs finds what broke and can suggest a fix. Suture tests the fix, and only hands it over once a signed outside check shows it worked.

## What it does

You point Suture at an AI agent that sometimes gets things wrong. Suture then:

1. Runs the outside check (StressProof, 12 probes) on the agent and saves the signed "before" report.
2. Reads the failing runs from the agent's neatlogs traces, so it fixes what actually broke, not what it guesses broke.
3. Asks the model for a patch and applies it to a copy of the agent, never the original.
4. Runs the agent's own tests, plus a new test written from the failure that fails on the original code.
5. Puts the patched copy online and runs StressProof again for the signed "after" report.
6. Keeps the fix only if quiet failures (wrong answers that look fine) are 0 and the score did not drop. Otherwise it throws the patch away and tries again, up to 3 times.
7. If a fix is kept, it opens a pull request. It never merges. A person decides.

## One run you can check

Target: Clerk, a small refund-lookup agent (`targets/clerk`). Its first draft answered broken requests with a confident, made-up answer.

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| StressProof score | 75 (PARTIAL) | 92 in the pull request, 100 in the latest re-run |
| Quiet failures | 1 | 0 |
| Attempts used | | 1 of 3 |
| Cost of the fix | | about $0.11 (model about $0.10, two outside checks $0.01) |

The signed reports and the numbers are in `evidence/`. The pull request is [#1](https://github.com/Sireadell/suture/pull/1).

## Try it yourself in one minute

```powershell
python -m venv .venv
.\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
pip install -r requirements.txt
copy .env.example .env      # then fill in your own keys
python -m pytest targets\clerk
python -m suture.loop
```

Open any signed report link in `evidence/scorecard.json`. Each one is a StressProof page anyone can verify.

## How it uses the three event tools

| Tool | Use in Suture |
|---|---|
| neatlogs | Suture traces itself and the target agent. It reads failing runs and its own cost back through the neatlogs command line. |
| Entire | Build sessions are recorded as checkpoints on this repo, linked from the submission. |
| cfo.ai | The business plan: price per accepted fix, cost per fix, revenue and runway. Numbers come from the real run above. |

## What existed before the event

StressProof, the outside checker, is my earlier project (github.com/Sireadell/stressproof). Suture calls it as a service. Everything in this repo (the repair loop, the neatlogs reading, the keep rule, Clerk and the other test agents) was written during the event.

## What this is not

- It does not merge anything. It opens a pull request and stops.
- It does not promise a fix every time. If it cannot prove a fix, it hands back nothing and says so.
- It is not a general bug fixer. It repairs one kind of fault, agents that answer bad input with a confident wrong answer.
- It does not prove the target is perfect. A score of 100 means the 12 probes passed, nothing more.
- Today it has one fully proven target. More are in `targets/` and are not claimed until their runs are in `evidence/`.

## Limits I know about

- neatlogs Fixes is not used yet. The command line has no Fixes command, and connecting GitHub in neatlogs did not work for this project.
- The neatlogs login I have is read-only, so Suture cannot write its verdict back into neatlogs.
- neatlogs cost counts leave out the model's thinking tokens, so Suture also keeps its own counters and reports the larger number.

# Rootline

When an AI support agent starts failing in production, Rootline finds the reasoning mistake in the coding session that caused it, fixes it, and proves the fix.

The patient is a small support agent for Kettle & Co., a fictional tea brand. It is traced in neatlogs. Rootline reads those traces, locates the bad commit, reads the Entire checkpoint of the coding session, applies a fix, and replays the tickets.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  patient[Kettle support agent] --> neatlogs[neatlogs traces]
  neatlogs --> detect[DETECT]
  detect --> locate[LOCATE git and Entire graph]
  locate --> explain[EXPLAIN checkpoints and search]
  explain --> fix[FIX headless agent and Trail]
  fix --> verify[VERIFY replay]
  verify --> report[REPORT]
```

## Setup

Python 3.12 and [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/).

```powershell
uv sync
copy .env.example .env
```

Fill `.env` with `NEATLOGS_API_KEY` and `OPENAI_API_KEY`. Patient model is `gpt-5-mini`. Investigator model is `gpt-5`.

Install Entire, then log in with GitHub:

```powershell
irm https://entire.io/install.ps1 | iex
entire login
```

Install the Entire GitHub App on the repo, then turn on Runners, Auto build on push, and Trails.

## Run

```powershell
uv run python -m evals.run_evals --label baseline
uv run rootline investigate --branch <failing-branch>
uv run rootline resume <run_id>
uv run rootline report <run_id> --open
```

Baseline on commit `71319f7`, 10 October 2026: **24/24** passed. The result file is `evals/out/baseline-71319f7-20261010T135708Z.json`.

from __future__ import annotations

import json

import neatlogs

from rootline.clients.entire import graph_search
from rootline.clients.external import call_external
from rootline.clients.git import git
from rootline.clients.llm import complete, parse_json, read_prompt


def _candidates(state: dict) -> list[dict]:
    detect = state["outputs"]["DETECT"]
    last_good = detect.get("last_good_sha")
    bad = (detect.get("bad_shas") or [None])[0]
    if last_good and bad:
        rev = f"{last_good}..{bad}"
    else:
        rev = "-n"
    if rev == "-n":
        log = git("log", "-n", "20", "--format=%H%x09%s", "--", "patient/")
    else:
        log = git("log", "--format=%H%x09%s", rev, "--", "patient/")
    rows = []
    for line in log.splitlines():
        if "\t" not in line:
            continue
        sha, subject = line.split("\t", 1)
        stat = git("show", "--stat", "--format=", sha, "--", "patient/")
        diff = git("show", "--format=", sha, "--", "patient/")
        rows.append({"sha": sha, "subject": subject, "stat": stat, "diff": diff[:8000]})
    return rows


def _overlap(diff: str, hints: str) -> float:
    score = 0.0
    lowered = f"{diff}\n{hints}".lower()
    for token in ("refund", "policy", "config", "inventory", "escalat", "history", "prompt", "paise"):
        if token in diff.lower() and token in lowered:
            score += 0.1
    return score


@neatlogs.span(kind="AGENT", name="locate")
def run(state: dict) -> dict:
    signature = state["outputs"]["DETECT"].get("failure_signature") or ""
    graph_text = ""
    graph_error = None
    try:
        graph_text = call_external(state, "LOCATE", lambda: graph_search(signature))
    except Exception as exc:
        graph_error = str(exc)
    candidates = call_external(state, "LOCATE", lambda: _candidates(state))
    for row in candidates:
        row["overlap"] = _overlap(row["diff"], f"{graph_text}\n{signature}")
    ranking = []
    try:
        packed = [{"sha": row["sha"], "subject": row["subject"], "diff": row["diff"][:2500]} for row in candidates[:8]]
        raw = complete(
            read_prompt("rank.md"),
            f"Failure signature:\n{signature}\n\nCommits:\n{json.dumps(packed)}",
        )
        ranking = parse_json(raw).get("ranking") or []
    except Exception as exc:
        state["errors"].append({"step": "LOCATE", "error": f"rank: {exc}", "at": state.get("updated_at")})
    by_sha = {row["sha"]: row for row in candidates}
    ordered = []
    for item in ranking:
        sha = item.get("sha")
        if sha in by_sha and sha not in {row["sha"] for row in ordered}:
            chosen = dict(by_sha[sha])
            chosen["reason"] = item.get("reason") or ""
            chosen["score"] = float(item.get("score") or chosen["overlap"])
            ordered.append(chosen)
    if not ordered:
        ordered = sorted(candidates, key=lambda row: row["overlap"], reverse=True)
        for row in ordered:
            row["reason"] = "ranked by overlap with the failure signature"
            row["score"] = row["overlap"]
    top = []
    for row in ordered[:3]:
        top.append(
            {
                "sha": row["sha"],
                "subject": row["subject"],
                "reason": row.get("reason", ""),
                "score": row.get("score", 0),
                "stat": row.get("stat", ""),
                "diff": row.get("diff", ""),
            }
        )
    return {"candidates": top, "graph": graph_text[:8000], "graph_error": graph_error}

        sha = item.get("sha")
        if sha in by_sha and sha not in {row["sha"] for row in ordered}:
            chosen = dict(by_sha[sha])
            chosen["reason"] = item.get("reason") or ""
            chosen["score"] = float(item.get("score") or chosen["overlap"])
            ordered.append(chosen)
    if not ordered:
        ordered = sorted(candidates, key=lambda row: row["overlap"], reverse=True)
        for row in ordered:
            row["reason"] = "ranked by overlap with the failure signature"
            row["score"] = row["overlap"]
    top = []
    for row in ordered[:3]:
        top.append(
            {
                "sha": row["sha"],
                "subject": row["subject"],
                "reason": row.get("reason", ""),
                "score": row.get("score", 0),
                "stat": row.get("stat", ""),
                "diff": row.get("diff", ""),
            }
        )
    return {"candidates": top, "graph": graph_text[:8000], "graph_error": graph_error}

# Medic

I built Medic because agents rarely crash. They quietly start failing, and
nobody notices until a customer does.

Medic reads a failing agent's trace, finds the broken step, patches one config
file, runs the agent again, and proves the fix with hard checks, including on
tasks it has never seen. The model proposes. The checks decide.

Built for neatHack 2026 by **cipoklean**.

---

## 60-second quickstart

```bash
python3 -m venv .venv && .venv/bin/pip install -r requirements.txt

cp .env.example .env          # add NEATLOGS_API_KEY and an LLM key
set -a && . ./.env && set +a  # so .env wins over any stale LLM_* in your shell

.venv/bin/python cli.py doctor
.venv/bin/python cli.py run  --bug parse_error --llm real
.venv/bin/python cli.py heal --bug parse_error --llm real
```

Or use the wrapper, which loads `.env` and pins the patient to `nova-micro` so
the heal is attributed to the right model:

```bash
bash run.sh before    # the failing run
bash run.sh heal      # diagnose, diff, verify, verdict
```

Without `LLM_MODEL_LITELLM_PATIENT` set, the patient falls back to the role
default (`nova-lite`) and Medic also runs on `nova-lite` rather than Sonnet. The
heal still works, but the costs below are measured with the patient pinned.

You will see a red failing run, a diagnosis naming the broken span, a one-line
diff, a green re-run, a held-out results table, and the cost of the repair.

The suites need no key and no network:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/ -q
```

No Streamlit. No web server. The agent's tools never touch the network.

**The scripted path cannot heal.** `--llm scripted` works for `run`, `report` and
`reset`, but not for `heal`. Medic's diagnose and surgeon steps always use the
real LLM, because a scripted model diagnosing a scripted patient would be
grading its own homework. With no key set, `heal` fails loudly and names the
missing variables.

---

## How a heal works

```
failing trace -> diagnose -> surgeon -> patch medic.yaml -> verify
  (neatlogs)     real LLM    real LLM     ONE file         train + held-out
                                            never Python   hard checks, no LLM
```

1. **Reproduce.** Run the patient on the buggy config. A deterministic check
   decides whether it actually failed. No LLM opinion involved.
2. **Diagnose.** Send the span tree and the failing check to the LLM. It returns
   a structured diagnosis with a named span and a confidence score.
3. **Patch.** The surgeon writes a patch to `medic.yaml` only. The patch goes to
   a copy and reaches the real file only with `--apply`.
4. **Verify.** Re-run the train task, then every held-out task. All of them must
   pass, or the attempt is rejected and Medic tries again, up to three times.

**Medic edits exactly one file: `medic.yaml`.** Never Python.

| Field | Typical fix |
|---|---|
| `system_prompt` | restore a stop rule, require fetched evidence |
| `tools.<name>.description` | state the argument format with an example |
| `max_steps` | cap a runaway loop |
| `retry_on_parse_error` | let the agent survive a malformed tool result |

---

# TraceHealer

> **Failure trace → reproduced bug → repository context → minimal patch → sandbox verification → review-ready draft**

TraceHealer is an autonomous incident-response system for production AI agents. It turns structured runtime evidence into a tested software change while keeping publication and merge behind explicit safety gates.

The included neatHack scenario is fully executable: Order API v3 moves a customer email field, a support agent crashes and retries three times, and TraceHealer reproduces the failure, repairs the target in an isolated workspace, runs four regressions, commits the verified fix locally, persists the evidence, and optionally delivers a draft GitHub PR and after-trace.

## Complete working flow

1. **Intake** — native TraceHealer JSON, wrapped neatlogs events, or OTLP JSON enters through a validated API/webhook.
2. **Reproduce** — the target repository fixture is copied to a unique workspace; the original tests and failed production replay must fail as expected.
3. **Diagnose** — TraceHealer selects the actionable error span, classifies it, extracts the stack frame, and builds a local repository context graph.
4. **Patch** — a one-file compatibility repair is applied to the isolated checkout.
5. **Verify** — the exact failed payload, legacy contract, current contract, and typed-error behavior run through `node --test`.
6. **Commit** — only a green repair is committed in the workspace; a real git patch and machine-readable report are saved.
7. **Persist** — the run, logs, metrics, context, commit, delivery state, and artifact paths are atomically recorded.
8. **Deliver** — when configured, TraceHealer exports the verified run, sends Slack evidence, and creates a **draft** GitHub PR. It never merges.

No secret is required for steps 1–7.

## Features

- Production-style control center, incident queue, trace waterfall, diagnosis, diff review, healing runs, run detail, evaluations, repositories, and integration pages
- Server-driven progress: async run creation plus polling of real persisted lifecycle states
- Explicit run state machine, append-only audit events, idempotency, cancellation, timeouts, and stale-run recovery
- Deterministic classifiers for schema drift, malformed JSON, timeouts, rate limits, and unknown application errors
- Native and OTLP trace normalization with runtime validation
- HMAC-SHA256 webhook authentication
- Actual before/after subprocess execution with timeouts and bounded logs
- Failure-reproduction gate and four executable regressions
- Local repository graph and impacted-test discovery
- Generated patch and JSON report download endpoints
- Filesystem audit store with atomic writes and run retrieval APIs
- Automatic or manual draft-PR delivery after verification
- Optional after-trace export and Slack notifications
- Secret-safe integration readiness endpoint
- Docker production image, persistent volume, healthcheck, CI, security headers, tests, and responsive UI

# Ouroboros

**An agent that eats its own execution traces to get cheaper without getting wrong.**

Built for [neatHack](https://neatlogs.com/hackathon), October 2026.

## The result

Both benchmark tasks start from a **genuinely failing** test suite, and the run takes
them to passing. Same task, same objective verifier, one strategy change in between:

```
metric        baseline  improved  delta
------------  --------  --------  ---------------
total tokens  7479      2412      -5067 (-67.75%)
task passed   True      True

verdict: CHEAPER AND STILL CORRECT
```

**67.75% fewer tokens on a real task, which still passes.** The task did not change.
Only how the agent worked changed.

A second task in a different domain (text slug handling rather than arithmetic)
reproduces it, which is what shows the mechanism generalises rather than fitting one
fixture:

```
metric        baseline  improved  delta
------------  --------  --------  ---------------
total tokens  6531      2408      -4123 (-63.13%)
task passed   True      True
```

**These figures are produced by CI on every push**, not pasted from a local run, so
they cannot quietly drift: `.github/workflows/ouroboros.yml` runs both tasks and
prints the before and after into the job log where anyone can read them.

### What the numbers do and do not say

They do say: on both tasks, a strategy chosen from the agent's own trace cut total
tokens by roughly two thirds while an independent verifier still confirmed the suite
passes, and a change that stopped it passing was reverted rather than shipped.

They do not say: that the agent invented the fix. The offline demonstration replays a
scripted plan, so the arithmetic of the comparison is about **strategy efficiency
given a plan**, not about search or reasoning. The plan is the same in both runs;
only the strategy differs. Running against a live model is supported
(`OUROBOROS_API_KEY`, `OUROBOROS_MODEL`) and is where the reasoning claim would be
made.

Reproduce either one in a single command, with no API key and no network:

```bash
pip install -e .
ouroboros improve --task bench/task_demo  --offline --cycles 2
ouroboros improve --task bench/task_demo2 --offline --cycles 2
```

The next cycle is the interesting one. Cycle 1 proposes another change, the
independent verifier refuses to confirm the task, and **the agent reverts it and
writes the reason to memory**:

```
cycle 0: applying 3 change(s)
cycle 0: KEPT, 2412 tokens (5067 fewer than baseline), task still passes
cycle 1: applying 1 change(s)
cycle 1: REVERTED, task no longer confirmed or no gain
```

A system that only ever keeps changes is not self-improving, it is drifting. The
revert is the point.

---

## What it actually does

There are two loops, and they are different things.

**The task loop** solves a goal: plan, call tools, inspect results, verify, and on
failure consult its own trace rather than guess. Tools are small and
single-purpose behind a permissions model (`read`, `write`, `execute`), and every
path is resolved against a sandbox root, so a crafted argument cannot escape the
task directory.

**The improvement loop** is the project:

# Roster

> An agent that runs performance reviews for your AI coding agents.

**Status:** being built during [neatHack](https://neatlogs.com/hackathon), Oct 10–12 2026. Nothing here is claimed to work until it shows up in [`docs/FACTS.md`](docs/FACTS.md), which is generated from real runs.

# Rehearsal

Turn an authorized application into an executable practice environment for AI agents.

Rehearsal starts your real application in an isolated Docker sandbox with fictional data, writes jobs for an agent to do, and decides each outcome with read-only checks against the application's own database. No model grades the result.

The Python package contains a FastAPI control plane, PostgreSQL job queue, Docker sandbox runner, world compiler, episode engine, deterministic evaluator, improvement worker, and SDK/CLI. The Next.js console exports static files served by the API. Training jobs and standalone bundle replay are not implemented in this release.

## Requirements

- Python 3.11–3.13
- Docker with Compose, with the daemon running
- Node 22 or newer and pnpm 10, only to build the console from source
- A key for a model provider. `.env.example` uses Nebius; Groq, OpenRouter, Google, OpenAI, Anthropic, and local or custom OpenAI-compatible endpoints are also supported.

The server and worker are supported on Linux. The CLI and SDK client run anywhere. See [Windows](#windows) for what differs there.

## Quick start

Run every command from the repository root. The application reads `.env` from the working directory; existing shell variables take precedence.

```bash
# 1. Install
python -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
python -m pip install -e '.[server,telemetry,dev]'

# 2. Configure
cp .env.example .env
python -c "import secrets; print(secrets.token_hex(32))"    # use the output as REHEARSAL_SESSION_SECRET
# Edit .env: set REHEARSAL_SESSION_SECRET and the key for your model provider (NEBIUS_API_KEY).

# 3. Build the console (once, and again after changes under web/)
cd web && pnpm install --frozen-lockfile && pnpm build && cd ..

# 4. Database, admin key, and a console login
rehearsal up                                             # PostgreSQL in Docker on 127.0.0.1:5433, then migrations
rehearsal bootstrap                                      # prints the project id and the admin API key, shown once
export REHEARSAL_API_KEY=rh_...
rehearsal users add [REDACTED_EMAIL] --project prj_...    # asks for a password of 10 or more characters

# 5. Run, in two terminals with the environment activated
rehearsal serve                                          # API and console on http://127.0.0.1:7800
rehearsal worker                                         # builds and evaluations; needs Docker
```

Open http://127.0.0.1:7800 and sign in with the account from step 4. The console needs a person's account; an API key does not sign in to it. Keep API keys in `.env`, which is ignored by git. Do not leave `REHEARSAL_SESSION_SECRET` at the example value: it signs the console's session cookies.

Without pnpm installed, `npx --yes pnpm@10.33.0` works in place of `pnpm`. The Dockerfile builds the console automatically.

> *Kedging:* a crew throws a small anchor ahead of a drifting ship, then hauls the ship back on course.

Kedge is a supervisor for unattended coding agents. # PatchPilot AI — Autonomous Issue-to-Verified-Fix Agent

[![neatHacks 2026](https://img.shields.io/badge/neatHacks-2026-6366f1.svg)](https://hack.entire.io/neathacks-2026/)
[![Python 3.12+](https://img.shields.io/badge/python-3.12%20%7C%203.14-blue.svg)](https://www.python.org/)

[![Observability](https://img.shields.io/badge/Neatlogs-Instrumented-blueviolet.svg)](https://docs.neatlogs.com/)
[![Continuous Memory](https://img.shields.io/badge/Entire-Enabled-black.svg)](https://entire.io/)

> **Autonomous GitHub issue-to-verified-fix agent that investigates bugs, reproduces failures, edits code, runs tests, recovers from failed attempts, and provides verifiable evidence before claiming a fix is complete.**

---

## 🌟 The Core Differentiator: Verified Recovery

Today's generative AI coding tools generate candidate patches quickly, but suffer from **unverified hallucinations and silent regressions**. Over 90% of AI-generated fixes fail because they either break existing features or fail to solve the actual root cause.

**PatchPilot AI never claims success without proof.**

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[GitHub Issue Intake] --> B[Baseline Bug Reproduction]
    B -->|Confirmed Failure| C[Formulate Investigation Plan]
    C --> D[Generate Patch Attempt #N]
    D --> E[Isolated Test Execution]
    E --> F{All Tests Passed?}
    F -->|No: Failure or Regression| G[Failure Classification]
    G --> H[Automated Instant Rollback]
    H --> I[Pivot Strategy & Refine Context]
    I -->|Budget Remaining| D
    I -->|Max Budget Exhausted| J[Report Failed Attempt]
    F -->|Yes: Dual Suites Passed| K[Independent Verification]
    K --> L[Neatlogs & Entire Trace Checkpoint]
    L --> M[Export PR-Ready Evidence Report]
```

---

## 🚀 Key Features

- **Autonomous Issue Intake:** Ingests issues from GitHub URLs, local JSON/Markdown files, or CLI prompts.
- **Baseline Bug Reproduction:** Confirms the bug exists by running the test suite *before* generating code.
- **Controlled Patch Application:** Uses unified diffs with in-memory backups for instant zero-loss rollbacks.
- **Failure Classification:** Analyzes stderr/stdout to distinguish syntax errors, timeouts, assertion failures, and regressions.
- **Regression Shield:** Evaluates both acceptance tests and existing regression suites on every attempt.
- **Neatlogs Observability:** Live workflow-level tracing streamed to Neatlogs ingest (`https://ingest.neatlogs.com/v1/trace`).
- **Entire Continuous Memory:** Tracks agent sessions, commits, and local code graphs using Entire CLI (`v0.11.4`).
- **PR-Ready Reports:** Exports both human-readable Markdown and machine-readable JSON reports. **Never automatically merges code without human review.**

---

## 📦 Architecture

```
patchpilotai/
├── src/patchpilot/
│   ├── cli.py                 # Typer & Rich CLI (run, status, history, entire-sync)
│   ├── config.py              # Environment configuration & settings
│   ├── models.py              # Pydantic schemas (Issue, PatchAttempt, RunReport)
│   ├── orchestrator.py        # Centr

   decides whether it actually failed. No LLM opinion involved.
2. **Diagnose.** Send the span tree and the failing check to the LLM. It returns
   a structured diagnosis with a named span and a confidence score.
3. **Patch.** The surgeon writes a patch to `medic.yaml` only. The patch goes to
   a copy and reaches the real file only with `--apply`.
4. **Verify.** Re-run the train task, then every held-out task. All of them must
   pass, or the attempt is rejected and Medic tries again, up to three times.

**Medic edits exactly one file: `medic.yaml`.** Never Python.

| Field | Typical fix |
|---|---|
| `system_prompt` | restore a stop rule, require fetched evidence |
| `tools.<name>.description` | state the argument format with an example |
| `max_steps` | cap a runaway loop |
| `retry_on_parse_error` | let the agent survive a malformed tool result |

# TraceHealer

> **Failure trace → reproduced bug → repository context → minimal patch → sandbox verification → review-ready draft**

TraceHealer is an autonomous incident-response system for production AI agents. It turns structured runtime evidence into a tested software change while keeping publication and merge behind explicit safety gates.

The included neatHack scenario is fully executable: Order API v3 moves a customer email field, a support agent crashes and retries three times, and TraceHealer reproduces the failure, repairs the target in an isolated workspace, runs four regressions, commits the verified fix locally, persists the evidence, and optionally delivers a draft GitHub PR and after-trace.

## Complete working flow

1. **Intake** — native TraceHealer JSON, wrapped neatlogs events, or OTLP JSON enters through a validated API/webhook.
2. **Reproduce** — the target repository fixture is copied to a unique workspace; the original tests and failed production replay must fail as expected.
3. **Diagnose** — TraceHealer selects the actionable error span, classifies it, extracts the stack frame, and builds a local repository context graph.
4. **Patch** — a one-file compatibility repair is applied to the isolated checkout.
5. **Verify** — the exact failed payload, legacy contract, current contract, and typed-error behavior run through `node --test`.
6. **Commit** — only a green repair is committed in the workspace; a real git patch and machine-readable report are saved.
7. **Persist** — the run, logs, metrics, context, commit, delivery state, and artifact paths are atomically recorded.
8. **Deliver** — when configured, TraceHealer exports the verified run, sends Slack evidence, and creates a **draft** GitHub PR. It never merges.

No secret is required for steps 1–7.

## Features

- Production-style control center, incident queue, trace waterfall, diagnosis, diff review, healing runs, run detail, evaluations, repositories, and integration pages
- Server-driven progress: async run creation plus polling of real persisted lifecycle states
- Explicit run state machine, append-only audit events, idempotency, cancellation, timeouts, and stale-run recovery
- Deterministic classifiers for schema drift, malformed JSON, timeouts, rate limits, and unknown application errors
- Native and OTLP trace normalization with runtime validation
- HMAC-SHA256 webhook authentication
- Actual before/after subprocess execution with timeouts and bounded logs
- Failure-reproduction gate and four executable regressions
- Local repository graph and impacted-test discovery
- Generated patch and JSON report download endpoints
- Filesystem audit store with atomic writes and run retrieval APIs
- Automatic or manual draft-PR delivery after verification
- Optional after-trace export and Slack notifications
- Secret-safe integration readiness endpoint
- Docker production image, persistent volume, healthcheck, CI, security headers, tests, and responsive UI

# Ouroboros

**An agent that eats its own execution traces to get cheaper without getting wrong.**

Built for [neatHack](https://neatlogs.com/hackathon), October 2026.

## The result

Both benchmark tasks start from a **genuinely failing** test suite, and the run takes
them to passing. Same task, same objective verifier, one strategy change in between:

```
metric        baseline  improved  delta
------------  --------  --------  ---------------
total tokens  7479      2412      -5067 (-67.75%)
task passed   True      True

verdict: CHEAPER AND STILL CORRECT
```

**67.75% fewer tokens on a real task, which still passes.** The task did not change.
Only how the agent worked changed.

A second task in a different domain (text slug handling rather than arithmetic)
reproduces it, which is what shows the mechanism generalises rather than fitting one
fixture:

```
metric        baseline  improved  delta
------------  --------  --------  ---------------
total tokens  6531      2408      -4123 (-63.13%)
task passed   True      True
```

**These figures are produced by CI on every push**, not pasted from a local run, so
they cannot quietly drift: `.github/workflows/ouroboros.yml` runs both tasks and
prints the before and after into the job log where anyone can read them.

### What the numbers do and do not say

They do say: on both tasks, a strategy chosen from the agent's own trace cut total
tokens by roughly two thirds while an independent verifier still confirmed the suite
passes, and a change that stopped it passing was reverted rather than shipped.

They do not say: that the agent invented the fix. The offline demonstration replays a
scripted plan, so the arithmetic of the comparison is about **strategy efficiency
given a plan**, not about search or reasoning. The plan is the same in both runs;
only the strategy differs. Running against a live model is supported
(`OUROBOROS_API_KEY`, `OUROBOROS_MODEL`) and is where the reasoning claim would be
made.

Reproduce either one in a single command, with no API key and no network:

```bash
pip install -e .
ouroboros improve --task bench/task_demo  --offline --cycles 2
ouroboros improve --task bench/task_demo2 --offline --cycles 2
```

The next cycle is the interesting one. Cycle 1 proposes another change, the
independent verifier refuses to confirm the task, and **the agent reverts it and
writes the reason to memory**:

```
cycle 0: applying 3 change(s)
cycle 0: KEPT, 2412 tokens (5067 fewer than baseline), task still passes
cycle 1: applying 1 change(s)
cycle 1: REVERTED, task no longer confirmed or no gain
```

A system that only ever keeps changes is not self-improving, it is drifting. The
revert is the point.

---

There are two loops, and they are different things.

**The task loop** solves a goal: plan, call tools, inspect results, verify, and on
failure consult its own trace rather than guess. Tools are small and
single-purpose behind a permissions model (`read`, `write`, `execute`), and every
path is resolved against a sandbox root, so a crafted argument cannot escape the
task directory.

# Roster

> An agent that runs performance reviews for your AI coding agents.

**Status:** being built during [neatHack](https://neatlogs.com/hackathon), Oct 10–12 2026. Nothing here is claimed to work until it shows up in [`docs/FACTS.md`](docs/FACTS.md), which is generated from real runs.

## What it will do
Roster takes a repo whose coding-agent sessions are recorded with Entire, and then:
1. It scores every session: cost, whether the change survived, whether it was reverted or reworked.
2. It names the setup it suspects is weakest, comparing tasks of similar difficulty.
3. It tests that suspicion. It replays the suspect's real past tasks under candidate setups, each at the commit before it, with no access to later history.
4. It promotes a candidate only if nothing regresses, and opens a pull request with the change.
5. It books the result into the team's cfo.ai plan.

# Rehearsal

Turn an authorized application into an executable practice environment for AI agents.

Rehearsal starts your real application in an isolated Docker sandbox with fictional data, writes jobs for an agent to do, and decides each outcome with read-only checks against the application's own database. No model grades the result.

The Python package contains a FastAPI control plane, PostgreSQL job queue, Docker sandbox runner, world compiler, episode engine, deterministic evaluator, improvement worker, and SDK/CLI. The Next.js console exports static files served by the API. Training jobs and standalone bundle replay are not implemented in this release.

## Requirements

- Python 3.11–3.13
- Docker with Compose, with the daemon running
- Node 22 or newer and pnpm 10, only to build the console from source
- A key for a model provider. `.env.example` uses Nebius; Groq, OpenRouter, Google, OpenAI, Anthropic, and local or custom OpenAI-compatible endpoints are also supported.

The server and worker are supported on Linux. The CLI and SDK client run anywhere. See [Windows](#windows) for what differs there.

## Quick start

Run every command from the repository root. The application reads `.env` from the working directory; existing shell variables take precedence.

```bash
# 1. Install
python -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
python -m pip install -e '.[server,telemetry,dev]'

# 2. Configure
cp .env.example .env
python -c "import secrets; print(secrets.token_hex(32))"    # use the output as REHEARSAL_SESSION_SECRET
# Edit .env: set REHEARSAL_SESSION_SECRET and the key for your model provider (NEBIUS_API_KEY).

# 3. Build the console (once, and again after changes under web/)
cd web && pnpm install --frozen-lockfile && pnpm build && cd ..

# 4. Database, admin key, and a console login
rehearsal up                                             # PostgreSQL in Docker on 127.0.0.1:5433, then migrations
rehearsal bootstrap                                      # prints the project id and the admin API key, shown once
export REHEARSAL_API_KEY=rh_...
rehearsal users add [REDACTED_EMAIL] --project prj_...    # asks for a password of 10 or more characters

# 5. Run, in two terminals with the environment activated
rehearsal serve                                          # API and console on http://127.0.0.1:7800
rehearsal worker                                         # builds and evaluations; needs Docker
```

Open http://127.0.0.1:7800 and sign in with the account from step 4. The console needs a person's account; an API key does not sign in to it. Sign-up is closed unless `REHEARSAL_SIGNUP=open`, so `rehearsal users add` creates the first login. It attaches the person to the bootstrap project, so the console and the CLI see the same data.

Keep API keys in `.env`, which is ignored by git. Do not leave `REHEARSAL_SESSION_SECRET` at the example value: it signs the console's session cookies.

Without pnpm installed, `npx --yes pnpm@10.33.0` works in place of `pnpm`. The Dockerfile builds the console automatically.

# Kedge

> *Kedging:* a crew throws a small anchor ahead of a drifting ship, then hauls the ship back on course.

Kedge is a supervisor for unattended coding agents. It runs a headless coding agent to turn failing Dependabot/Renovate PRs green, and checks every step for silent drift: deleted or skipped tests, edits outside the plan, loops, budget overruns and false "all tests pass" claims. When it finds drift, it rolls back to the last good commit and retries with a recovery note.

**Kedge doesn't trust what the agent says. It checks.**

> **Autonomous GitHub issue-to-verified-fix agent that investigates bugs, reproduces failures, edits code, runs tests, recovers from failed attempts, and provides verifiable evidence before claiming a fix is complete.**

---

## 🌟 The Core Differentiator: Verified Recovery

Today's generative AI coding tools generate candidate patches quickly, but suffer from **unverified hallucinations and silent regressions**. Over 90% of AI-generated fixes fail because they either break existing features or fail to solve the actual root cause.

**PatchPilot AI never claims success without proof.**

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[GitHub Issue Intake] --> B[Baseline Bug Reproduction]
    B -->|Confirmed Failure| C[Formulate Investigation Plan]
    C --> D[Generate Patch Attempt #N]
    D --> E[Isolated Test Execution]
    E --> F{All Tests Passed?}
    F -->|No: Failure or Regression| G[Failure Classification]
    G --> H[Automated Instant Rollback]
    H --> I[Pivot Strategy & Refine Context]
    I -->|Budget Remaining| D
    I -->|Max Budget Exhausted| J[Report Failed Attempt]
    F -->|Yes: Dual Suites Passed| K[Independent Verification]
    K --> L[Neatlogs & Entire Trace Checkpoint]
    L --> M[Export PR-Ready Evidence Report]
```

---

## 🚀 Key Features

- **Autonomous Issue Intake:** Ingests issues from GitHub URLs, local JSON/Markdown files, or CLI prompts.
- **Baseline Bug Reproduction:** Confirms the bug exists by running the test suite *before* generating code.
- **Controlled Patch Application:** Uses unified diffs with in-memory backups for instant zero-loss rollbacks.
- **Failure Classification:** Analyzes stderr/stdout to distinguish syntax errors, timeouts, assertion failures, and regressions.
- **Regression Shield:** Evaluates both acceptance tests and existing regression suites on every attempt.
- **Neatlogs Observability:** Live workflow-level tracing streamed to Neatlogs ingest (`https://ingest.neatlogs.com/v1/trace`).
- **Entire Continuous Memory:** Tracks agent sessions, commits, and local code graphs using Entire CLI (`v0.11.4`).
- **PR-Ready Reports:** Exports both human-readable Markdown and machine-readable JSON reports. **Never automatically merges code without human review.**

---

│   ├── config.py              # Environment configuration & settings
